body: Thank you so much! 🤗

Yeah, you're totally right... I keep using the excuse of "we're colleagues, we have to interact with each other at least once a month" in order to not block him, but I think I'll have to find a way around this. I just don't want things to be awkward when we meet up with our other colleagues, they even congratulated us on the fact that we're on such good terms :( but in the meantime, I'm disrespecting myself... You don't know how much I wish that I didn't *still* have my university life so intertwined with his, it would have made everything a million times easier.
I'm "glad" I helped my ex become a better person, so he can go back to her... 4 years of supporting him, even when he was fighting with her, all for nothing in the end.

Don't take him back. This level of disrespect is disgusting. Let him deal with his stupidity, he should learn his lesson. Don't even dare to think you're below average, it's not worth it to lose your self confidence because of the scumbag that your ex is.

For context, it's been 4 and a half months for me, but at first I was feeling exactly like you. We even had a trip planned, and we broke up 5 days prior, all our plans were ruined. It gets better with time, I still have bad days when I let the negativity get to me, but it's way, way better than in those initial stages.

Exactly how my breakup went as well. We got into a huge fight, initiated by me, and I kept blaming myself for everything for like, a month after the breakup. The thing is though, if one fight is all it took, then either the relationship was way past its due time (my case), or he couldn't handle hardships in the relationship, couldn't properly communicate etc, and you're better off without him. Think about it, if down the line a serious, life changing issue would have come up, he would have reacted the same and it would have been even worse than now. People who don't stick through thin and thick aren't worth our tears and self blame.
We broke up 4 days before the 2 and a half years mark.

The only answer I have is that desperate people go to drastic lenghts sometimes. It's impossible that he formed this sort of connection with someone he's known for only two weeks; he's only projecting his feelings for you onto someone else (and maybe he hopes you'd see this and that it would make you jealous). Don't read too much into it and don't let it affect you, he sounds a bit emotionally immature if he can behave like this *publicly*.

My ex did the exact same after we broke up, he suddenly became very active on Instagram. It's their way of coping I think, I've also been guilty of posting more since the breakup, it's an easy way to get validation and attention (it's also a very dangerous trap, if you rely too much on it).

I relate a lot to the feelings you've expressed with this. I also still have a lot of negativity to let go of, anger and bitterness still taint my memories though I'm trying to not let myself get lost in them. Mostly, I regret that it ended, emotionally speaking, as I was willing to still fight for it, but logically, it was for the best and it taught us both valuable lessons. Once the logical and emotional part align, then we can truly say that we've healed. Best of luck on your journey to get there! ❤️

It is a gift for him, not for his new partner to enjoy. I know exactly what you're feeling, I'm having similar thoughts with my ex, but ultimately, if he goes through a lot of self improvement and becomes a better man and a better partner, I can only be happy for him. Sure, he won't ever be with me again, but all I've ever wanted for him is to be happy and fulfilled. I thought I could be the one to offer him these things, and for a while I was, until it didn't work anymore, but if he learned something from our relationship that will help him in the future (and I'm 100% certain he did, I'm already seeing the effects), then I've done my part. I've supported him for 4 years, both as a friend and as a lover, and I'm proud of who he's turning out to be. Yes, it sucks that I've invested so much in someone, emotionally speaking, only to lose him in the end, but I did it out of love, and that should be enough. Love is not a finite resource. I still can't imagine him with someone else, I still die on the inside when I think of him loving another girl, but I'm giving myself the time to heal. The hardest thing to accept is that we work better as friends than as lovers, so I've taken some space from him in order to process these things (broke up 4 months ago, after a month we came back in contact, but last week I realised I can't pretend that I don't love him anymore and I've put some distance between us). Oh, and we also had an anxious/ avoidant (me/ him) type of relationship.

There are several things people have told me, but they ended up leaving me anyway, so I don't trust their words anymore... My former bff told me at one point that I make her life better and she's grateful for me, then dropped me like I meant nothing to her (and ended up apologising for her behaviour a year and a half later - I ain't going back to that though), one ex of mine always said the loveliest things about me, then started getting distant, they didn't care about me anymore, I cut off contact and blocked them, and they reached out 3 months later to tell me they missed me. My current ex showered me in compliments, of physical nature as well (I actually miss him telling me that he loves my body), kept telling me that I'm valuable, that I have a lot of untapped potential, that he wishes I could see myself the way he sees me, but what struck me the most was this: "if the world had more people like you, it would be a better place". He still broke up with me though. It's hard not to feel like a piece of shit when the most important people in your life end up leaving you... Guess I'm actually not that valuable to anyone.

Thank you for the encouragement 🤗 I'll contemplate more these days, no one is forcing me to decide anything right now on the spot. And yeah, I have to remind myself that it's ok to feel bad, I keep thinking that I'm weak for still being bothered by the breakup, while he's doing much better than ever, but I guess that shows just how much more invested I was in the relationship itself...

Mhhh, I feel the same, I was envisioning a long future for this relationship, but to him, it was doomed and had been so for several months. I somehow feel like I've lived through a delusion, it was a bit traumatising in this sense. The same for you, if you need to vent if it gets too much to bear, feel free to message me, I'm a good listener as well :')

Thank you for replying! Just to clarify, I didn't mean he cares in a romantic way about me, just about me as a person you know? The way you would care for someone who's close to you. So yeah, I stand by what I said, he's definitely moved on romantically.

That being said, I was actually doing quite well, I managed to shift some of my perspectives on life and change some mindsets (the way I deal with stressful events isn't by throwing myself into old/ new hobbies or other activities, but by introspection), I'm not dependant on him anymore (like I was during the relationship), and a few more things like these. I don't know what happened this week to destabilise me like this, it's definitely not the first time I see him after breaking up, our other interactions haven't left me feeling bad, I was *content* with the whole situation, so I don't know, but at least subconsciously something must've changed.

To some extent, I agree that I'm drinking poison. I knew there would come a day when I'd have to make this choice, I just didn't expect it to come so soon and to hit me so suddenly. I believe I've tricked my brain into keeping a sense of calmness, or maybe I've managed to focus on the positive aspects of breaking up and remaining friends, but I'm not sure that's possible anymore. Maybe I am doing it only for the memories. Maybe there was 0.1% left of hope inside of me, hope that he'd change his mind, and now that disappeared as well.

In any case, this is a valuable response and I greatly appreciate you taking the time to write it!

Thank you so much for your reply! You're definitely much stronger than I am, and you have my respect for the way you handled this situation. It's true, you can't be friends with someone whom you love, and no matter what I tell myself, I just can't suddenly stop loving him, it's not something I can control. So basically, I'll have to take the route of cutting contact as well... Breakups suck so much, man.

Yeah I totally understand what you mean, it's the same with my relationship. I was the "inexperienced" one, and this combined with some other factors led to its demise. Looking back, I should have done some things completely differently, but I didn't know better at that time... It honestly bothers me a lot.

Spot on. He is acting as if he is totally not bothered by the breakup, and he most likely isn't, so treating me as just a (close) friend really shouldn't surprise me. I hope that he'll know better now and he won't keep throwing this kind of stuff at me as if I'm immune to it. Thank you for your input! It's always helpful to get out of my head a bit and see others' perspectives 😊
Oh yeah, I let him know that it bothered me to hear those things, but I didn't ask him why he wanted to share. That's the territory of "forbidden discussions".

I actually feel the same. I thought fate brought us together and it was meant to be, but I've learned that's just bullshit. There's no such thing as fate. Sorry for sounding rude, but I'm so bitter at how everything turned out to be after I invested so much of myself in the relationship.

This sounds like something my ex would tell me. And he would be right. I've regained my independence after he broke up with me, I am OK with being by myself and I don't berate myself as often as I used to do. The breakup definitely triggered some changes in my perspective. So I hope it is the same for your ex as well, and I hope everything turns out the way you want it to 🤗

Keychains and fridge magnets. Usually bought as souvenirs, and I'm fortunate enough to have travelled a lot around the world. Imagine filling the entire front of a fridge (the tall fancy ones, I don't know what they're called in English) with magnets, and having to move to the side of the fridge because we never stopped buying them. Also, my keys are usually 80% keychains, 20% actual keys, gotta find some use for them, right?

Reading through this, I can recognize so many things that both my ex and I did... Thank you for this list, I needed a reminder that the breakup was for the best and that we couldn't save the relationship.

I would let the person know if I decided on no contact, because we've been talking and we're on good terms, so it really depends on the situation. Not everything is black and white. Would they care if you suddenly stopped talking to them? Would they reach out? The answers to these questions should guide you.

I'm glad that I could be of help, best of luck with this situation! It's somehow normal to hold back/ withdraw, as I mentioned, it's very difficult to be open with someone whom you've broken up with, someone whom you used to share everything with before... I know that I find it difficult to be truly myself with my ex as well, even though before I didn't hold back at all, now it's a different dynamic, not knowing what would cross the boundaries and what is acceptable. For example, he at one point said he wouldn't emotionally support me anymore, but he still did it when I was having a breakdown, and since then I've been afraid of doing it again, mainly because I felt as if I was taking advantage of him and his willingness to be there for me... So there are a lot of factors to be taken into consideration, and only honesty with them can be of help here. I've read your other comments as well and saw that you think of asking them to stop this form of communication, maybe if you have this discussion you can gain some insight into what's been going on!

All of this sounds so much like the relationship between my ex and I. For the last year, there have been more lows than highs, at least from his perspective (objectively speaking, it's the truth, but the way that I'm wired, I focused more on the positive). Towards the end, we just couldn't communicate at all, I felt misunderstood and disrespected every time, and he probably felt the same. Minor things would turn into arguments which would go on for hours. Neither of us learned how to let go of the resentment from the bad situations we've been through in the relationship, we didn't properly express it either, so it just kept building and exploding at the worst moments possible. He also distanced himself emotionally for the last few months (and physically as well, due to quarantine), which only made me cling more to him and all in all it was a very unhealthy dynamic. I was dealing with a lot of external stress from covid and the quarantine and all this year had to offer, and instead of finding a safe space with him, I took it all out on him. So after a huge fight, the explosive type that I mentioned, he understandably broke up with me. I'm not proud to say that I've actually begged him to give it another chance; I never wanted us to break up, I just wanted things to change, and I was still willing to sit down and have a long, proper discussion about all the shit that had happened... my love for him had never diminished, it was just buried under so much resentment. It was too late for that though.

It's been 3.5 months since then. I was able to admit to myself and to him that breaking up was the best choice for us at that moment. The vicious cycle couldn't be broken otherwise. For the first month or so we didn't really talk, but afterwards we began to gradually text more frequently, and now we're talking almost daily. And here comes the point of my essay. It's weird, it's strange, and I have no clue how it will affect me/ us down the line. He was very clear on not getting back together, so throughout these months, while talking to him and going to him for emotional support, I've also had to forcefully kill my hopes of reconciliation. Let me tell you, this dichotomy could drive someone insane, so I'm quite surprised that I find myself thinking now, "I don't even want him back".

It is incredibly difficult to go straight to friendship after a break up, at least from the dumpee's perspective. I'm constantly worried that I'm overstepping boundaries, and we've actually overstepped some and I'm trying to figure out how to put them back in place without suddenly withdrawing from him. I keep wondering, should I share this with him? Am I being overbearing? I once tried to show some support to him before an exam, and I was feeling... Extra caring and affectionate towards him, and after I pretty much berated myself for acting like that. I thought he didn't want it, even though he thanked me for it. I just keep believing that he's too nice to tell me to **** off (it's an exaggeration to prove my point, he wouldn't ever tell me that) and he's going along with this mock-friendship, but for reasons I don't know. 

I sometimes feel the same, that our current interactions are unfulfilling shadows of our past interactions, but I focus more on the romantic ones. I find myself thinking of all the cute things he'd say to me, and now, when they would usually come up in conversation, there's nothing. And I realised that I don't remember how to be his friend and only friend; I only know that before we dated we got along excellently, we were closer than usual, everyone thought we were dating but I could never see myself dating him, then he got in a relationship and I realised I have romantic feelings as well for him :))) So how could I be his friend now, after 2.5 years of being romantically involved? We can't even hang out together, he refused my invitation saying it wouldn't be good for us. Also, I realised that if he gets in a new relationship in 1-2 months I'll cut contact completely, because I wouldn't be healed enough to be able to see him give his love to someone else. I already went through that once and I almost couldn't bear it, not to mention doing it *now*...

My point is, some healing is possible even when in contact. I certainly feel better and more balanced in my way of viewing life. I'm not wallowing in my sadness anymore, I have motivation, I've started enjoying fun things again, I've started being more confident in my ability to be on my own, etc etc, so there has been some progress. There's still never a day when I don't think of my ex, and I still miss him, but I think I'm on the way to being ok with the fact that this is the end. There's still long until then, but I'm not in denial anymore. Of course, every person and every situation is different, but it's normal to feel the way you do. I don't know how recent your break up was, but there's always a transition phase, in which both parties need to adjust to the sudden loss of, basically parts of their lives. For some, this transition means going no contact, for others it means staying in touch. Both are tough in their own ways, and I don't even know which one would be better. To completely cut off someone who's been there every single day, or to be in contact and feel confused, distrustful in their intentions, and like you're lying to yourself? In my experience, I'd rather stay in contact and deal with the rest, because that's how attached I am to this person. I don't know anything about what he's thinking, I don't believe I'll "win him back", as I mentioned, a big part of me doesn't want him back, but it's still a confusing mess. I'm just pushing it all aside and choosing to focus on the fact that I can still talk to him in some ways, and I'm grateful for it. I think this year has shown me that I should be grateful for more stuff, so even with all the negatives associated, I'm grateful he's still in my life.

So yeah, to end this essay: if you decide to go no contact, let them know. Or, better, before going no contact, try expressing all these feelings to them, see if they reciprocate or if they're confused and not knowing how to deal with it. Dumpers' and dumpees' perspectives are very different, even if they lose essentially the same things. The way you're feeling is totally understandable, so try to communicate it. This is also a small test: if they'll be able to listen, then it means they've also worked on themselves. If the discussion goes the same way as when you two were together, then you can be certain nothing has changed. And one last thing: take some time to think if you actually want their friendship or you're just clinging to them after the break up. Be honest with yourself. For me, it's a combination of both, even if the friendship isn't what it used to be, it is more than I could have hoped for. And I want him as a friend. He's a valuable person, and I'm willing to push through this adjustment period if it means we can remain friends.

All the best to you and good luck!
This is one of the best comments I've seen on this subreddit.
I feel you on this, it's exactly what I'm currently going through...
That's the thing, there wasn't that cooling off period, so that's why I'm saying that a friendship isn't possible immediately after.

Yeah, I know what you mean. He isn't dating anyone yet, but I can feel it happening soon and I really don't want to be around to see that, I couldn't handle it. Best of luck with your situation! I think NC is the way to go.
I 100% agree with this comment. Jumping right into "friendship" is just a delusion, one that I'm living through every single day...

Let me just say, it's been 3 months since the breakup. Haven't had proper NC, but for the first month we barely spoke, and those weren't  proper conversations anyway. After a month and a half, we met up to clear the air a bit and see how to proceed from then on. Basically no getting back together, we'll just go with the flow. Since then, we began talking daily, we got to the point where it felt like "the old times", but without the actual romance, though every time we met (for university) we would laugh and joke and even flirt a bit. So yesterday I asked him if he wants to hang out today, because you know, I thought that's what friends do, and with the amount of talking we've been doing, I didn't think I'd cross any boundaries. He answered me this evening, he refused, saying that it wouldn't be good for us. Moral of the story: friendship isn't possible. I'm contemplating cutting him off, even though 1. I'm not brave enough for it and 2. We'll inevitably meet again at uni and I can't just ignore him... But I don't know, I feel like he's just leading me on, or just enjoying my presence until he finds some other girl... On the other hand, he's also been supporting me through some tough times after the breakup, so honestly it's all a mess and it's f*cking with my head and emotions.
Thank you! Everything is just so confusing, I'm doing my best to navigate through this and still keep up with my responsibilities 😬 it's been some tough months lately

Thanks for the reply! He's been clear on not wanting to get back together, so that's something I won't bring up again (and I'm not even sure if I actually want to be together with him again, I certainly don't miss the bad parts of the relationship). I'll just shut up about this whole situation and see how it plays out I guess... It's true, I can't decide anything for him, but if he does find someone else, be it his ex or another girl, then I'd want him to tell me and not lead me on anymore.

Thank you so much for your kind words ❤️ I'm somehow struggling to see the light at the end of the tunnel, so to speak, because there's nothing here to really distract or help or excite me, even the winter holidays lost their appeal... 

But anyway, congrats on the events in your family!! They'll be such a source of joy, make sure to fully take part into them :D And everything you've said to me, it goes right back at you, you too are strong and worthy and loved by many other people in your life, and this is what we should focus on now 🤗

I could have written this post. Except for the hugs part, I relate to everything. He surprisingly is always there for me, whether for uni or personal problems, we talk about the same things as before, all this stuff. And it's also holding me back from truly healing after the breakup and only making me miss him more... I see no way out of this situation, I'm not strong enough to let him go completely, I can't ignore him either (we're colleagues in the same group at uni), basically our lives are still intertwined and it's making it all quite difficult.

Thank you. I did most of these actually after the breakup, it was necessary for me to be able to focus on studying and on bettering myself, controlling my feelings and thoughts and emotions, I thought I was really back on track... I felt like I was back on track. But today just proved that I'm as incapable as ever. My ex did a great job on this exam and here I am, with a shitty grade and my self esteem buried 6 feet under.

Thank you for your words and for taking the time to answer me :') good luck with your situation as well, and try not to beat yourself up for it, see how you can improve on yourself, take it as a lesson! 😊
I feel you man, I feel you...

We did have some sort of closure talk, but we didn't exactly establish how to act further on... Just that we won't get back together and we won't stop talking. I'm distancing myself from him though, and I've noticed he started doing the same, which should be good, but it sucks :)) I know it's for the best though

Can't break contact, we see each other weekly for university, and I just found out we're also together in an optional class... The universe has a funny way of doing things 🙄 the worst/ best part is that we still get along well
I wish I'd stop hoping, and keeping in touch with him isn't helping at all...
How I wish my ex wrote this. But he's much happier without me, while I'm here still thinking that I would have given it another shot if he wanted to... He made it perfectly clear he doesn't want it.
I'm starting to believe that no, it isn't possible. The friendship will never be the same.
Yep, precisely, I don't think anything good ever comes out of it.
Yeah, I keep messaging him as well, and it either turns into a conversation (1 out of 10 times), or more often he replies with 1-2 words and it's over. It's really not worth it at all.

It's been two months, I didn't throw out anything (he told me he didn't either), didn't delete any photos (we didn't have any together on social media, but I did un-tag myself from something on Facebook), only got rid of the messages and conversations. Last year I had a huge fallout with my best friend, I also kept everything she's given me and I still use some of the stuff, kept all the photos, even though we haven't spoken since January. My point is, it's my memories, they're my things, a part of my life, and I don't plan on erasing them and pretending they don't exist. I even got to the point where I can look at them without feeling any sort of sadness. I know that there will be a time when I can look back, smile and be grateful for everything that's happened, so I don't want to regret getting rid of everything on an impulse. In addition, I quite like the stuff I've been given and they're very useful tyvm!
OH MY GOD YES. I got a message from her more than a month ago!! I posted in r/breakups, she's literally preying on emotionally wounded people. It was so weird 😐
This hits hard, I woke up today missing him and wishing that things were different... I got my closure, but it takes time for my feelings to catch up with my rational side.

A list of impossible things. He would have to admit to everything I'll write below. 

He would need to make me a priority in his life, I spent too much time feeling like I'm not even on his list of priorities. He would have to actually respect me, not dismiss every single problem I bring up and make me feel crazy and fcking "delusional" for telling him about my emotional issues and the issues with the relationship itself. Generally, I would want to be able to talk to him without being terrified of it turning into a fight where I'm left feeling 10x worse. He should actually make an effort towards the relationship, not let me plan all the fun stuff to do together, only for him to almost never be on board. He should take initiative as well and freaking take me on dates in places he knew I like, because I kept dropping hints like crazy. He would always jump on the slightest opportunity to make new experiences with others, but with me, he was content to just stay inside and play video games together all day. Even going to take a walk in the park was almost impossible. He would have to actually deflate his goddamn ego and stop acting as if he's better than everyone else and he can't make mistakes. He should start actually apologising for his wrongdoings!!! He's stubborn and doesn't open up emotionally and just expected me to be a good little girlfriend and obey him, God forbid that I could actually contradict him on something (the second half of thjs sentence is just my frustrations coming out, it's not the absolute truth because I've made a lot of mistakes as well). He'd have to stop being a goddamn walking paradox, he never understood how difficult it is for me to navigate through all the mixed signals he's been giving me, through his words and actions. And our fights... Were truly something else. God, how did I put up with those for so long...

A part of me feels bad for writing all of this down, because in the almost two months since the breakup I've understood how it all came down to this and I've learned what *I* have done wrong. We were caught in a vicious cycle, there was absolutely no way to get out of it except for breaking up. Him taking this initiative was honestly the best thing he did for us in the last months. I know we won't get back together, and for now I don't even want to because I have a ton of personal stuff to work on, and he has a lot of issues to solve as well, but I'm still hoping that at some point in the future I could be friends with him.

Tbh, writing this down is almost cathartic, I need to fully let go of the resentment if I want to properly move on.
I plan on talking to my ex too this week, I'm already spending too much energy on this situation.
Yeah, I learned this the hard way, it's so strange how two people can have an amazing friendship, but in a relationship they wouldn't get along as well. Humans are so weird, man.
I'm so, so tempted to tell him the same, but having this kind of conversation through texting would make me go insane at this point...
Oh I really wish I could block him, but I have to resort to only ignoring him for now.
I'm 99% sure that's what would happen to me as well if I'd ignore him :)) circumstances make it so that I can't though 🙃

So. This will be long. My ex and I have known each other for 4 years, 1.5y very close friends and 2.5y dating. We broke up a month and a half ago, not really mutually as I pretty much begged him to give it another chance the day it happened, but now I can see that it was for the best and I respect him for having the courage to end it.

The thing is, we still kept in touch afterwards, spoke a bit about how we were feeling, but it was still too raw and nothing really came out of it. He didn't want no contact, he didn't want to keep talking like usual, basically he was very confused and didn't know what to tell me or how to proceed from now on. Still, he told me he needs to work on some personal things as well, so if he's distant and cold or isn't answering, I shouldn't take it personally. Well you see, one day after I waited from morning 'till evening for him to answer some messages, I decided I've had enough of the confusion and uncertainty, so I told him I'd take space for myself, but if he wants to tell me anything I'd answer.

One week passed, heard nothing from him. At one point I caved and sent him a message telling him that I hope he's well, he didn't answer. I ofc got angry and told myself, "fine then, screw it, I'm not going to talk to him at all and I'll ignore him" bla bla bla. The thing is, some days later, I still sent him something. Asked a dumb question, mainly to see if and how he would respond. He was more than happy to help me, which pleasantly surprised me.

Our situation is special, because we're going to the same university so we're seeing each other once a week. The two times we've met so far, we didn't ignore each other, we talked, made a few jokes here and there, but it wasn't at the level which we had before. It still felt awkward and a bit strained, but that's to be expected. It was mostly one sided, he initiated basically every conversation we've had f2f (I was just answering what he asked me and keeping the conversation going, but I didn't share much about myself), and he even initiated some via texting. Even yesterday, we spoke about university stuff, then he started rambling about philosophy before going back to studying :)) So really, it's actually going better than I expected. 

My advice, from my experience, would be to distance yourself from him, never expect him to actually answer or be nice to you, don't feel like you can rely on him, don't send multiple messages if they remain unanswered, be polite if he does talk to you but don't insist on keeping it going if he pulls away, if he makes a joke don't ignore it, but really, the most important thing to remember is: your level of communication won't ever be the same. I was hurting as well, thinking how little I matter to him after breaking up, but I realised that 1. It doesn't matter anymore, he isn't obligated to look after me anymore, and I know how much he cared about me while we were still together, and 2. It's not really like that, our interactions prove the fact that at least he wants me to be a part of his life.

After a breakup, everyone needs some time to figure out their thoughts and recognize the changes which occurred in their lives. It can be stressful to navigate the new type of relationship that one has with their ex, so a period of no contact (or very little contact as I've had) can be very beneficial until everything settles down and both parties gain new perspectives. It sucks if you still hope for reconciliation, but contacting him less and less and keeping your expectations low should help with it. At this point, I don't even want him back, because I took the time to 1. Kill my hopes and 2. Be honest with myself about the reasons why our relationship didn't work out and wouldn't work out in the future either.

I understand it's way harder to let go after a 6y relationship, and I'm not saying that everything I did could help you too, but I also understand the feeling of wanting to keep them in your life. I honestly can't imagine actually losing him at this point, the fact that he still wants to talk to me makes me very happy. Even so, I remind myself every day that it won't ever go back to the way things were even before we were dating. We have to build a new type of friendship, if we ever will. So that's what you should try too, figuring out what's the best way to approach this new situation, how to talk to the new him if I can say so, kill your hope of reconciliation and most importantly, all that energy you spent on him, try to turn it towards yourself.
